posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Another thing about the Adept is the sheer number of ways he can help other heroes. He has a grand total of two means of dealing damage (Scherzo fo Frost and Flame, and the Accompany of erm, Syncopated Onslaught, I think), and if I ever use one of them it's only because I have literally nothing else I can possibly use. Oh, and one time I used one of those to get the kill on Akash'Bhuta, just because I could ;). But the Adept is all about support, and in opinion even more so than, say, Legacy or Visionary. Pair him up with, say, Unity ("Oh, you can't play bots on your turn? Okay, play one on mine…in fact, I'll sing that song again - okay, now you can play another one"), and it can get pretty epic. Similarly, you can let someone re-use a power that they just played on their own turn - Legacy and Galvanise, for example - he can use it on his turn to give everyone a +1 to damage, but then it's the Adept's turn and he can get Legacy to use it again for a total of +2 damage. And then supposing someone like Tachyon or Jim is next…>:)

You seem to have a thing about his stuff getting destroyed. He can use Vernal Sonata and/or Instrumental Conjuration to get some of it back, or Arcane Cadence to gamble on what's in the top five cards of his deck. There aren't that many villains who destroy everything - most only destroy a fixed number of cards across all heroes, or belonging to the hero with the highest/lowest hp, so the Adept doesn't even have to lose anything. Then again, because he has so many different effects he can access via songs, and because, as with any hero, some of those effects are pretty situational, it means that if you've got nothing better to do you can just put out a song you know you probably won't be using, just as something you can freely throw away if some ongoing destruction comes out. And if someone else loses a card they really wanted to keep, just chuck out a Vernal Sonata to let them get it back again…albeit not till the end of their next turn, unless they get to draw before then. I do seem to recall a game in which Fanatic had played Wrathful Retribution. So now it's in the trash. I (the Adept) play Vernal Sonata, and suggest that Fanatic puts Wrathful Retribution on top of the deck. During my Power phase, I use the Accompany of Counterpoint Bulwark to let her draw it. I can't remember if I then used Alacritous Subdominant or Inventive Preparation to let her play it as well, or whether she did so on her turn. Either way it was an extra play of the card and was probably enough to finish off the villain (though I can't remember those kind of specifics as it was ages ago ;)).

I'm curious as to why you keep saying about the card names not meaning anything to you, or suggesting what the card actuall does. Does "Inspiring Presence" suggest +1 damage and a one-off +1hp for everyone, for example? Or would you know, at a glance, that Hypersonic Assault nerfs all damage coming from stuff it hits, as opposed to erm…the one that deals the same damage but has no other effect? The cards have to have some kind of name, after all ;). Anyway, I tend to focus more on the image than on the name of the card (it took me a while to remember the names for all the Adept's cards because they use quite long words, but I've got it now and I think they're cool anyway), which is why I've not been able to get too attached to any of the upcoming Vengeance cards when playing in games that use those - all except the character cards just have a blank white space where the image is gonna be. Still, it's something to look forward to when it actually gets released :).

If you're not a fan of support characters (or just the Adept in general), that's fine, of course. I'd love to play him in a game with you, though, and show you what kind of stuff he can do :). I gather you play most of your games solo? That might be why you seem to have trouble getting the hang of some of the characters (coupled with the fact that you've not had the game long, of course ;)), since you're having to focus on all the decks at the same time, rather than being able to let other people manage their own heroes and stuff. Playing with someone who's got more experience than you might help you pick up the numbers quicker in terms of not missing stuff because they'll know the decks better and know what to watch out for, and stuff :). And also, you'll see how other people play certain characters. You might have developed your own preferred method of playing a certain hero, but then see someone else playing the same hero in a completely different way and go "Hey wow, I never thought of doing that", and get a whole new perspective on how to play them and stuff :).

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
Some heroes are more situational than others, and that will always be the case.  I've been playing for a while, and I'm still figuring out how to play different heroes, and finding situations where one hero completely dominates in a way that I never understood before.

I don't take issue with your assessments- because they are your personal assessments, and its totally OK to have different opinions on different heroes.

Here are some things to try/think about, if you want a different perspective on heroes.

 

Mr. Fixer- He's incredible.  It takes a ton of patience and time to master him, but its worth it.  Having a jack handle in any situation where you have to hit yourself is good times!  One of my most satisfying games was with Mr Fixer destroying all of Apostate's relics (irreducible damage+jack handle+bloody knuckles) and leaving him open for everyone else.  It really helps to either maintain a very "play what you have, not what you want" mindset...or to pair him with Team Leader Tachyon so that you are more likely to HAVE what you need!   

 

Bunker- Bunker is one of those characters that I'm still working on.  I have phenomenal games where I save everyone, I have terrible games where I can't get set up or spend turn after turn drawing and feel like I'm letting the team down.  I can say that he's a master of the waiting game.  He's got great armor potential, and if you can find satisfaction in spending some time waiting, armoring up and taking the hits...Bunker can reward with some really fun blasts.  Or you can literally spend the entire game in recharge mode with heavy plating, absorbing hit after hit with a Gatling gun and Omni-cannon, charging and whittling.  I'm still learning him, and I've played a LOT of games.  I don't feel like I've figured him out, but i feel like I'm finally beginning to be effective with him.

 

Wraith- I spend more time with Wraith peeking at the villain deck with the eyepiece and debuffing them than actually shooting.  She's great at combat, but she's absolutely phenomenal at arranging things and getting a massive array of options while doing it.  If you feel that damage is king, and its every hero's responsibility to pile it on, she certainly can, but that barely scratches the surface.

 

Fanatic- I really don't understand your perspective on Fanatic.  thats OK, but its entirely contrary to my perceptions of her.  We've had games where End of days turned the tide, and wrathful retribution was Fanatic's last, desperate attack.  we've had times when Final Dive got rid of one of Voss's guards so that everyone else could do damage again, or when embolden let someone pull off some ridiculous tricks with dual powers.  Or divine focus burning through (reduce the first hit each turn) armor so that everyone esle could be effective. 

 

the Argent Adept- I rarely play him, because there are always other people who want ot play him more.  He's phenomenal as long as he survives.  Much has been said already, so i won't add much beyond how much flexibility he adds to any game.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
I am planning on trying out the combination of Adept and Unity sometime (when I want a party that broken), as the two of them are sort of half-homages to Green Lantern, my second or third favorite superhero.  Together, they can doubtlessly accomplish a lot, but I won't want to waste that kind of raw power on a weak villain who never destroys their stuff, as it's just too degenerate when build-up heroes like that are able to operate unchecked.

Ameena:

You seem to have a thing about his stuff getting destroyed. He can use Vernal Sonata and/or Instrumental Conjuration to get some of it back

Conjuration only gets Instruments, which are useless without songs (and in my experience, Ongoings seem to get destroyed more than Equipment - Citizen Dawn is a notable example, having one way to destroy Equipment but three for Ongoings).  And Sonata doesn't give you a play for the turn, so when you have your turn begin with all your songs destroyed, you play Sonata to get one back, but it'll be next round before you can play it, and meanwhile you've wasted the opportunity to draw two cards on your turn by playing a card when you didn't have a power to use.  Destruction really hurts the Adept, and yes it is often destruction of everything.

There aren't that many villains who destroy everything - most only destroy a fixed number of cards across all heroes, or belonging to the hero with the highest/lowest hp, so the Adept doesn't even have to lose anything.

I played him against Matriarch, who got Huginn and Muninn in play, in a three-player game.  Later I played against Miss Information, who is similarly fearsome, although Adept wasn't in that game.

I do seem to recall a game in which Fanatic had played Wrathful Retribution. So now it's in the trash. I (the Adept) play Vernal Sonata, and suggest that Fanatic puts Wrathful Retribution on top of the deck.

I have never seen anyone play that except to kill a boss.  They hang onto it until Fanny is down to about 5 HP, by which time the boss is usually down to 20 or so, and if Fanatic survives (or is resurrected by an Aegis), then the party wins.  This is one of the reasons why I don't really like Fanny; she's too much of a spoiler for otherwise hopeless matches, and IMO it feels lame when she busts out a win from out of nowhere.

I'm curious as to why you keep saying about the card names not meaning anything to you, or suggesting what the card actuall does. Does "Inspiring Presence" suggest +1 damage and a one-off +1hp for everyone, for example?

Kinda, but more to the point, the HP healing happens the moment you play the card, while the +1 to damage is easy to remember because Legs is handing out Galvanize effects which have the same effect.  You just remember "Legacy is boosting all our damage", and then glance over to see if he has the card (with easily recognizable art) which indicates that it's automatic, &/or if you have to wait for his power phase for him to hand out "hats" (my word for status markers).

Or would you know, at a glance, that Hypersonic Assault nerfs all damage coming from stuff it hits, as opposed to erm…the one that deals the same damage but has no other effect?

Having played Tachyon about five times, yes I do know that one by heart, since it's such an incredible bacon-saver in tough games.  Also, again, it's a One-Shot; those are never terribly hard to remember.

The cards have to have some kind of name, after all

The more evocative and specific that name is, the better.  I actually once got a short-term writing gig with Wizards of the Coast to assign names and flavor text to cards.  I was extremely good at it, but the relationship ended due to a conflict with management.  (Shocking, I know.)

Anyway, I tend to focus more on the image than on the name of the card (it took me a while to remember the names for all the Adept's cards because they use quite long words, but I've got it now and I think they're cool anyway), which is why I've not been able to get too attached to any of the upcoming Vengeance cards when playing in games that use those - all except the character cards just have a blank white space where the image is gonna be.

Agreed with this; art is huge to me as a way to recognize cards, which is part of why I don't play with proxies of the promo heroes.  And the Adept is not the best in terms of illustrating his effects, given that it's difficult to draw a sound.  Offhand, I can only remember the healing thing, Sarabande of Destruction, Scherzo of Frost and Flame, and Cedistic Dissonant by their art (oh, and Supertonic because of the robot Baron Blade).  I know I had Syncopated Onslaught out as well, but its picture didn't seem to depict anything in particular as far as I recall, and I only know its name because you just mentioned it, although I do remember it as the only way for Adept to do more than 1 damage (except against Akash'bhuta).

I gather you play most of your games solo? That might be why you seem to have trouble getting the hang of some of the characters (coupled with the fact that you've not had the game long, of course ;)), since you're having to focus on all the decks at the same time, rather than being able to let other people manage their own heroes and stuff.

Yep, it's definitely a challenge…but that's part of what keeps me fixated on it.  Something of a masochist, I am…  I eagerly look forward to the day that I can finish a game, solo or otherwise, absolutely certain that I did not make one rules mistake.  It has yet to happen.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Finally tried the Argent Adept out in a non-solo game, and I can say that I recognize how he has a fair bit of potential, but I still don't really consider him to be for me.  It's virtually impossible for him to accomplish much in the first couple turns, and he has to luckily draw one of his super-powerful songs (chiefly Alacritous and Inspiring) before he can really get the ball rolling.  Combined with the tricky-to-memorize song-typing and the low starting HP, he's just got a very steep hill to climb, and doesn't feel like he pays off anywhere near as well for all his buildup and fiddlyness, compared to Nightmist or Omnitron or the Scholar, all of which are comparably difficult but offer much more immediate and powerful rewards.  If I were in the mood to play a cheerleader, I'd get more out of Argent than Legacy (as my list reflects), but I am seldom in that mood.

Meanwhile I did another solo run with Nightmist, and I've further confirmed that I really, really like her, although I'm still not sure she quite deserves my top spot.  Playing her is burdensome, as she always has to sacrifice a ton of potential power in order to actualize her options; it feels like work, and I feel like my #1 spot ought to go to a character who's just flat-out enjoyable at all times, but that's a tall order of course.  Scholar is probably closest to my definition of perfection, but still a bit awkward at times.  Also, Tachyon is beginning to feel simplistic to me (though still flat-out fun, unlike Ra, who I'm struggling to remain interested in despite loving the Egyptian feel), and probably doesn't deserve to be ahead of CR or even AZ anymore.

Omnitron probably deserves to switch tiers with Expatriette, as he's just tons of fun to me, although he still suffers enough shortcomings that I don't think he can take top billing...he probably gets the highest marks of any single hero for me, but also a lot of demerits that keep him from retaining the high score.  Also, Mr. Fixer is beginning to grow on me, though I'm still infuriated about Riveting Crane (if Fixer can manage to deal damage at all, why bother making it irreducible for anyone else?) and Meditation (I nearly always draw multiple Styles and Meditations, with maybe one Tool).  He should have a tutor for his tools, since he doesn't have to destroy those when switching them.  Lastly, while I didn't play Bunker today, my very smart friend Thorin did...and he went into Turret Mode with Flak Cannon and Grenade Launcher out, just as I always do.  Unless you fail to draw these cards, I fail to see how it doesn't eclipse all his other options, so I still consider him a depressingly linear character, with a lot of potential that almost always goes to waste.

So, a few adjustments to the list, but it's still pretty much accurate.  I can't wait until Vengeance arrives and I'll be able to shake these rankings up a little.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
The Adept doesn't need multiple cards out to be useful - he can be amazing with just one, depending on what it is. Inspiring Supertonic? Okay, TLT would you like to use your base power so everyone can draw a card? Or maybe Legacy wants to stack a second Galvanise on top of that first one he just cast so Fanatic will be dealing 3+3 damage with her base power on her next turn? Alacritous Subdominant? Okay, Mr Fixer how about you play that Overdrive that's in your hand so you can use Strike twice right now? Or Unity, perhaps you'd like to put out that Turret Bot so he can shoot at someone when your turn starts? And so on. Some songs are less useful, yes, but plenty can be pretty effective on their own, depending on what kind of options the other heroes have. A lot of what the Adept can do is more…indirect - he doesn't do much to the villain himself but he can let one of his friends kick the crap out of them (or get set up) faster :).

On the subject of Bunker, another set-up for him can be Heavy Plating, Recharge Mode, and the Omni-Cannon. Then you get to draw three cards a turn and have pretty good soak so can tank a lot while you charge up your Omni-Cannon. Okay so you're not really actively doing much, but it's certainly a viable alternative to the Turret Mode one, and satisfying if you get to totally obliterate the Big Bad with a most-of-your-deck-loaded Omni-Cannon :). There are other ways to play Bunker too, but those are probably the main ones.

Phantaskippy has pretty much summed up why Riveting Crane is good on Mr Fixer - if he has a damage buff to get through someone's soak, he can enable everyone else to whack them pretty well too - after all, if he has a damage buff, in many cases other people will too (eg if the buff is coming from something like Galvanise), which means said buff will be even more effective on those other people as it won't be needed to help burn through the target's soak.

Basically, every hero has their strengths and weaknesses. Some will get their arses totally kicked in some circumstances whilst seeming almost obscenely overpowered in others. That's just the way it goes, and is kind of the point of the game - it encourages the players to think about what they're doing and plan their tactics together and stuff. If one hero is having trouble right now (say, Jim or Tachyon because the villain has a pint or two of soak), then another can help them out (maybe Legacy can buff their damage, Mr Fixer with his Riveting Crane and self-buffs can get through the soak and remove it for everyone else, etc). You don't have to do even a single point of damage to be a super-effective hero (eg Visionary, the Adept), nor do you have to be constantly hammering away at them with everything you've got (Ra, Haka). Once you get to learn the decks, you know which cards to keep an eye out for in order to set up the best combos (eg Taiaha does more damage than Mere, but Mere lets you draw a card and fill up your hand to do a massive Haka of Battle later on).

And even when you get a strategy you like with a character, you might then play a game with someone else and see them play that same character a completely different way, thus giving you new insights into how they can be effective :D.

posts.cooked:

On the subject of Bunker, another set-up for him can be Heavy Plating, Recharge Mode, and the Omni-Cannon. Then you get to draw three cards a turn and have pretty good soak so can tank a lot while you charge up your Omni-Cannon. Okay so you're not really actively doing much, but it's certainly a viable alternative to the Turret Mode one, and satisfying if you get to totally obliterate the Big Bad with a most-of-your-deck-loaded Omni-Cannon :).

You would have to know that neither the Villain nor the Environment is capable of destroying your Omni-Cannon.  (By the way, is there an explicit rule in the game about cards like Omni-Cannon, saying that when they're destroyed, the cards under them also go to the trash?  It's common sense, but It ought to also be stated specifically.)  And personally, I kind of disapprove of using that sort of meta-knowledge in the game.  Like, I'll probably never fight Plague Rat on Mars, because courtesy of one of the players on this board, I know that Meteor Storm completely shuts him down and lets the heroes sit there building up until they can kill him in one turn.  That this occurred once is hilarious, but to ever do it again would be utter lameness IMO.  (If I play him there at all, it will be with a small number of carefully selected heroes, who are not especially likely to be able to pull off this rather unfair upset.  No unity, no Ra and/or AZ, no Chrono-Ranger, no Legacy…perhaps I could do it with, like, Visionary and Scholar and the Argent Adept.

Phantaskippy has pretty much summed up why Riveting Crane is good on Mr Fixer - if he has a damage buff to get through someone's soak, he can enable everyone else to whack them pretty well too - after all, if he has a damage buff, in many cases other people will too (eg if the buff is coming from something like Galvanise), which means said buff will be even more effective on those other people as it won't be needed to help burn through the target's soak.

Yeah, all this is Cloud Cuckooland to me.  In my experience, what happens is that you're sitting there with your little 1-damage Strike, drawing an opening hand of Riveting Crane, two Harmonies and maybe a Grease Gun, and Warlord Voss starts the game with two Gene-Bound Guards in play, or the Dreamer has a Dark Hero, or Dawn has Citizen Anvil…it's almost comedic how regularly this sort of thing occurs in my experience.  I never count on being able to get an ideal setup; I want a character who's almost incapable of going wrong when the worst happens.  (Then again, I like Absolute Zero.  Go figure.)

And even when you get a strategy you like with a character, you might then play a game with someone else and see them play that same character a completely different way, thus giving you new insights into how they can be effective :D.

I have yet to observe this, save perhaps with Fanatic.  The guy I know who really likes her nearly always ends a game with Wrathful Retribution, whereas when I play her, I always seem to get first-turn End of Days and then plink away with Exorcism and a few One-Shots while hoping to draw Absolution.  (And, annoyingly, usually drawing multiples of it.  I'm so much happier with the Staff of Ra because that can destroy itself.)

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
If you hold off playing anything just in case the villain (or environment) puts out something that'll destroy it, you'll just end up never getting set up and they'll eat you. Yeah, you might get unlucky and find that the villain destroys your stuff twice in a row, but most villains can't destroy all your stuff consistenyly - most just force the destruction of a few, or of the stuff belonging to a certain hero. If you can change who that hero is, you can get around it - Autumn is destroying the Adept's stuff because he has the lowest hp? Okay, let's let Tachyon get hit a bit so she's got less hp than him and is much less likely to suffer from her stuff being destroyed because she's hardly got any and can get to the stuff she does have pretty quickly when she needs it because she goes through her deck so fast.

I don't think any character is, as you put it, "incapable of going wrong when the worst happens". For starters, "the worst" varies between heroes. Everyone's stuff has been destroyed? Bunker, Expatriette, and friends are probably rather annoyed while Tachyon isn't that bothered. Everyone getting hit for a load of damage? Whoops, there go Omni-10's components because he had the wrong plating out, meanwhile Legacy, Bunker, and Haka all sat there and tanked it. Everyone having to discard two cards? Again, Tachyon's probably happy with that, while the Adept and Omni-10 probably aren't that bothered. Bad news for Mr Fixer, though!

Also, you need to remember that if some of your stuff gets destroyed, there are those who can help you get it (or some of it, at least) back - Mr Fixer can play a Salvage Yard for all the equipment-heavy guys, while Tempest and the Adept can play Reclaim from the Deep and Vernal Sonata, respectively, to help everyone stick a single card back on top of their deck to draw next round (or possibly right now, if it's the Adept's turn), meanwhile Jim has multiple ways to find whatever he needs from his deck and/or trash :). Even the environment can help - destroying the annoying Evasive Red Dust on Mars lets everyone take a piece of equipment from their trash and put it into play when it gets destroyed.

We've had games where we were relutcant to play stuff in case it got destroyed, but that just resulted in none of the heroes really getting set up and we never tend to do very well in that case (barring those heroes like Tachyon who don't need many cards in play to be effective). Some villains who nuke your stuff can be handled pretty well, though - once had a game against Miss Information where I played Omni-10 and I practically soloed her as I got all my stuff out, including the right plating to block the repeated Psychic damage I'd be taking, while I think the other heroes were the ones to lose less important cards (though I tend to have no problem losing stuff like Rocket Punch, which I very very rarely use - I mainly stick to the components but other stuff is a nice bonus, like Bio-Engineering Beam, which for some reason I don't see very often). Fun game :D.

posts.cooked:
La Capitan has 2 copies of plunder.  Even with the boat you are not talking about a statistically likely occurance.  A first turn plunder isn't a bad thing either, since without any crew it destroys exactly 1 card.  Even with the boat out it would have to play Raiding party and then follow that with plunder, at which point with her normal destruction it would destroy (H) cards.

We aren't talking about highly likely circumstances.  Yeah it will happen, that's the game.  But to plan for something with under 5% likelihood of occuring, that isn't cautious, it is paranoid.

As for Autumn and Dawn, Dawn is going to blow you up eventually, but you can't live in fear of that, and Autimn is nasty if she's protected, but like stated above you can even smack an ally to get Autumn off of a specific hero.  You don't try to get in front of Dawn's destruction though, since it isn't a numbers game.

These scenarios are one of the reasons I really love Fixer and Expat.  Expat can really help a team get ahead of destruction, with a second card play, things like ammo to sacrifice and if you get speed loading, a free play to start your turn.  Fixer laughs at equipment destruction with Salvage Yard.

Omnitron-X, Expat, Chrono Ranger, Bunker, Argent Adept, and to a lesser degree Wraith and AZ can assist in getting in front of destruction.

Players like Tachyon and Visionary do fine when villains destroy equips, but can rarely help you get out in front of the destruction, they are great against Dawn for that reason.  Visionary and Fixer are great vs. Dawn, because with those two you can pull ongoings and equips out of the trash, and neither require many cards to be rolling.

 

Certain heroes are better or worse vs. specific villains or environments.  That is one of the cool things about this game.  I don't view it as right and wrong heroes to take into a fight, but I love it because that is how comic book fights work, sometimes heroes get caught in the wrong place vs. the wrong villain and have to do their best to overcome.

To mark my 30th game last night, I made up a personal database of how often I've played each Hero, in what matchup and to what result.  (I can't easily get this information out of the statistics compilation, since this doesn't distinguish heroes I played from heroes someone else played in a game with me, so I made up my own form.)

Some interesting tidbits from this survey:

* I've played Haka five times, but only against three different villains - Baron Blade and Grand Warlord Voss on both regular and advanced, plus the Dreamer on regular.  Conversely, in six games Absolute Zero, Bunker, and Ra have never repeated a villain.

* I've played Chrono-Ranger in only three different Environments: Silver Gulch, the Final Wasteland, and once on Mars.  Bunker, Legacy and the Scholar have managed never to visit the same Environment twice.

* After five games each, Unity and Visionary have never been incapacitated.  (Granted the same was true of the Scholar until he played his sixth game...but he only died there because I royally screwed up, so I have every reason to expect that U&V will go 6-0.)  In the same number of games, I've gotten Fanatic killed four times and lost the whole game three of them.  Tachyon and Zero have also died four times, but that was in six games, and they won all but two of them.

* I have yet to play Nightmist or Mr. Fixer in a game with a number of heroes other than 4 (7 total games between them, one of which contained both, and was also the only game featuring Fixer which the heroes won).  This is not incredibly strange, since I play four-hero games about half of the time (trying to alternate from 3 to 5 and back to 3 again with 4 always in the middle), but it's still interesting as a happenstance.  The Argent Adept is the other hero besides Nightmist whom I've played only thrice, but he had a different number of compatriots each time.

* I have never played Absolute Zero second in turn order.  Bunker and Tempest have never gone fourth, and none of Chrono-Ranger, Tachyon or The Scholar have ever been third,   Not one hero has managed to play a different position (out of the twelve possible ones) in each of six games.

* Ra and Tempest have never been in a 4-hero game.  All but the first of my games with Tempest have had five heroes, while Ra has played in five three-hero games and a single fiver.  (This had a lot to do with my having played mostly three-hero solitaire with simple heroes while I was still learning the game.  But the Tempest thing must have been entirely accidental.)

I'll probably have a few more interesting items of note after I chart up exactly what heroes I've paired with what others during my solo games.  I know that I have a bad habit of buddying Haka with Absolute Zero, but that's the only correspondence I'm sure of offhand, though I feel as if I see the same pairings a lot.  As I get more games played, it'll no longer be likely for me to unintentionally stumble into these interesting patterns, as I'll be obsessively logging everything and striving to try out exclusively new combinations, in as balanced a fashion as possible; thusly, I felt I should enjoy the idiosyncracy of my early games while it lasts.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Have gotten enough additional experience playing each hero (except Nightmist, who I don't think I've upticked since making this list - she's at 3 games right now, while everyone else is at least 5 and some are as high as 8) that I'm revising the order a bit, as well as further subcategorizing into six tiers rather than three.

Tier 1 - All-Time Faves

* Scholar.  While occasionally awkward, his playstyle is rewarding to me on so many levels, and I just love the flavor of him.  There may not be a more fun or much-more powerful card in the game than Proverbs and Axioms, and I love the numerical minigame of figuring out how best to use "Get Out of the Way!".

* Chrono-Ranger.  I concede the point to whoever said before I'd really enjoy CR, because I really do.  Probably the only reason I don't put him at #1 is that he lacks a lot of effectiveness when he can't get a Bounty out early on.

* Nightmist.  I've decided that too many of the decisions she forces you to make are painful for me to call her my #1 hero anymore.  But she's still incredibly interesting to me.

Tier 2 - Excellent Fun

* Absolute Zero.  The high-risk high-reward nature appeals to me less than simply the fact that he has to jump through a few hoops to become effective; he's the simplest of the Complexity 3 heroes, and that puts him at a sort of sweet spot.  Also I love his personality, though some of his flavor text isn't ideal to me.

* Omnitron-X.  I love the complicated, builduppy heroes with nuclear potential, and I've had some spectacular Omnitron games which have made him shoot upward in the rankings.  He's not higher than he is because of a certain level of clunkiness he suffers, the general shortage of one-shots other than Reset, the multiple reshuffles that one forces, the brokenness of Bio-Engineering Beam which turns awesome cards like Anubis into lame anticlimaxes, the fact that Timeshift stops short of some of its ideally desireable applications by being unable to return the card to the top of the deck, and the mechanical silliness of being able to destroy other heroes' Equipment and even Omnitron's Components for Singularity and Self-Sabotage.  Lots of individual negatives, but the whole they assemble into is cool enough that they can largely be forgiven.

* Tachyon.  Still appeals to my more ADD tendencies.  She's just fun, has some of the most powerful cards, is easy to understand but full of nuances, and is a hilarious character.

Tier 3 - Highly Enjoyable

* Visionary. Still the intellectual, megalomaniacal heroine I love, with a lot of really cool cards that nobody else really duplicates.  I still dislike how badly she can gimp certain villains with Precognition and Suggestion (and for this reason, Dark Visi is absolutely the last of the promo heroes I will ever want to play), and her psychic damage one-shots are also underwhelming, so she's swingier than I wish she were and often fails to live up to her potential.  But just her build-in power automatically goes some distance to correct this shortcoming, as well as making her a great team enabler.  As long as I stay away from the matchups which prime her to be stupidly overpowered in a lame way, and concentrate on giving her opportunities to shine in a unique and satisfying way, she'll bring me much joy.

* Expatriette.  Not much to say beyond what I've already said.  I have had a game with her since my previous writing where she opened on a hand with three Ammo and no Guns, and that royally sucked.  Speed Loading should really be at least a 3x in her deck, more Arsenal Access would be nice, and the fact that there are more Quick Draws than cards to fetch with them is unfortunate, leading to late-game dead draws.  But she's still an enjoyably active character; I feel as if she was a prototype for Chrono-Ranger, and that he profits from the learning experience represented by her shortcomings.  I also love the backstory of her being an exile from the Citizens of the Sun who now plans to prove the deadliness of powerless humanity to her mother; that's great storytelling.

* Tempest.  So powerful, and with loads of options.  I recently pegged him as the one hero I would play exclusively if forced to do so, just because he is better-rounded than my other faves, with his only real weakness being low HP that keeps his bad games mercifully short.  His backstory is a little bland for me and some of his cards are a bit simplistic, but overall he's just extremely solid, and much harder to go wrong with than most heroes, which is a huge plus for me given my dread of bad shuffles.

Tier 4 - Somewhat Conditional Faves

* Ra.  Playing him more, I've found him to contain a satisfying number of additional nuances which help mollify his overall one-noteness, and so I don't feel so bad about resorting to him now and again, even though I always look for reasons to play a more sophisticated hero.

* Unity.  Still a great character whose shtick is theoretically cool, but hampered by fragility and an over-reliance on either luck or exploits, tending to succeed big or fail miserably with little middle ground.  Utterly failed in a recent outing against Iron Legacy, so I've got more of a sour taste for her than usual just at the moment.

* Haka.  I love love love the immense starting HP, and loading up on cards with Mere or Dominion is really fun.  The Hakas are his weak point, as I'm seldom impressed with the healing of Restoration and almost never want to bother with Shielding (though I really must remember to try him against Omnitron sometime, just in the hopes of having him Shield for 16 right before an Electro-Pulse Explosive goes off).  I also generally feel bad about drawing Elbow Smash, as it's just rather underwhelming compared to other cards.  And the whole Maori shtick doesn't do it for me, making much of his flavor text feel wasted...I'd rather hear more about how he adapts to life in the Western world (the general impression I get is "very well", but some more details about how he ended up teaching kindergarden etc. would be nice to have).

Tier 5 - Heroes I Find Lacking Somehow

* Wraith.  Has more depth than I've given her credit for, but not much more; it's often hard to find time to play around with an Infrared Eyepiece or Smoke Bombs when you could just blast for 8 with a Targeting Utility Throwing Razor setup.  Also, her Stealth power goes to waste with tragic frequency; she'll probably be the first hero for whom I try one of the alternate promos.  Still, a very good newbie hero that I still have a soft spot for.

* Mr. Fixer. He's actually trending up rather well compared to my previous games, just not well enough to gain ground as other heroes also uptick.  The asymmetry between his Tools and Styles continues to bug me, as I draw the latter more than the former with truly absurd regularity, and I still tend to find him high-investment-for-medium-reward, similar to the Argent Adept in that regard, but less interesting about it.  However, he remains effective enough, and just at the right balance point between straightforwardness and complexity, for me to still appreciate him.

* Bunker.  As with Wraith, he suffers from the fact that some of his least interesting options are too effective not to emphasize, at the expense of his more clever potential.  And I really wish he had more HP and more soak, in order to qualify for the sobriquet "The Indestructible".  Still, he's one of the heroes I anticipate the most improvement to in future games; he could end up in Tier 3 one day if I grow tired of Expat and Haka and so forth, as he has an amount of depth which they tend to lack.

Tier Six - Played Grudgingly For the Sake of Balance

* Argent Adept.  I've come to understand him more or less fully by now, and this has greatly improved my fondness for him, but not greatly enough to escape the bottom sixth (once the game contains KNYFE and possibly Parse, we'll talk; both of those, from what little we know about them, have the potential to disinterest me).  He's extremely draw-dependent; I've had the "Arcane Cadence into Arcane Cadence" opening now, and it makes so huge a difference in his effectiveness as to leave me incredibly ennoyed he isn't guaranteed to get one in his starting hand.  Inspiring Supertonic is also an absurdly swingy card that gives his games a sea-change of effectiveness depending on whether or not it appears; overall, he's far too variable for my taste, and I still think is maximum potential is nowhere near as impressive as, say, Zero's or Haka's.  But he will likely continue to climb steadily in my esteem, even if he may never gain the momentum to exceed most other heroes.

* Fanatic.  Despite the whole Christian angle, I really want to like her.  Final Dive is one of the greatest cards ever, and the Divine Focus through Prayer of Desperation loop is magnificent...when I manage to play these cards in a game, I tend to enjoy her.  But she still has too many lame incremental one-shots like Brutal Censure, too many game-ending wrecking balls like End of Days and Wrathful Retribution (even as a singleton, that one nearly always seems to come up), and overall too little consistency to be worth putting up with her foibles.

* Legacy.  Still a dull cheerleader of a hero whose contributions to the game are seldom proactive enough for me (Take Down and Lead From The Front are great cards, but passively great, and that's not how I roll).  I like him best as a tank, but too many of his cards are situational at best, and his deck utterly fails as a Superman homage IMO, despite being a flavorfully interesting take on the concept.  I really need to try Young Legacy sometime, as she'll almost definitely be more my style, and Greatest Legacy might be even better, but the original is definitely just about played out for me.

More interesting (or at least I seem to think so) factoids from after my 40th Sentinels game, not counting the forum game that I jumped into after a couple of turns (which I'm not counting since I didn't pick out the villain and environment, nor did I choose my own Hero, and on top of that there were promos in it, which none of my other games have had).  As I become more aware of these statistical anomalies, it becomes less likely that they happened serendipitously, so eventually I'll stop bothering to observe them, but for now they still amuse me a bit.

* I've played every hero at least five times now (this requiring a somewhat painful night of back-to-back Nightmist games, neither of which was easy even apart from her involvement), and many are up to 8.  Haka still holds the record for fewest villains faced, at 4 different villains in his 6 games (tied with Nightmist, except she had one fewer game in total); besides the two 5s (Misty and Mr. Fixer), the only heroes never to repeat a villain are Bunker, Expatriette, Fanatic and Unity, with Uni being the only one to do this in seven games rather than six (many other heroes have faced seven villains in eight games).  This could easily be fixed by pitting the four of them against Omnitron, as all have gone up against him on either regular or advanced; counting regular and advanced versions of villains separately, however, they don't have a villain in common.

* Legacy is the only hero to have never repeated an Environment in eight games.  In the same number, Chrono-Ranger has only visited four; I seem to have a compulsion to keep sending him to Silver Gulch or the Final Wasteland, strictly for flavor reasons.

* The only hero I have never gotten killed is Nightmist.  Visionary and Chrono-Ranger are tied for the most games they didn't die in (7 each).

* I am uniquely terrible with Mr. Fixer; his five games have included three losses and a concession due to impatience.  (However, two of his defeaters were Chairman and Matriarch, so it's not entirely his fault.)  Conversely, not one of the games which included Omnitron-X was a defeat for the heroes, though he himself was incapacitated twice.  Expat and Fanatic currently have identical win/loss records - six games each, with four incapacitations and three team defeats.

* Fixer and Nightmist have still never been in a five-player game, not that this is incredibly strange since they've been in only five games period.  The same distinction is more peculiar on Unity, given that she's played seven times (and her eighth game is reserved for Freedom Six, so it'll remain true even then).  Absolute Zero and Fanatic remain ignorant of three-player games, and Ra has managed to get in eight games without ever being in a four-hero group, despite my playing that number roughly 45% of the time (three heroes is about 35% and five approximately 20, as I find threes much easier but tend to oscillate between fives and threes, with fours thus close to half of the total).

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Ameena:

I'm not too sure I'd ever refer to Megalopolis as "newbie-friendly", what with those Hostage Situations, Papparazzi, and Traffic Pile-Ups…

Those are actually a point in favor of the newbies understanding the game (not necessarily winning it, of course, although an easy villain on non-Advanced typically makes that probable anyway).  By skipping a phase, they briefly avoid the cognitive load associated with playing that phase; one of the best ways to speed up the learning process is to decrease the number of decision trees that must be mastered at one time.  And skipping a draw phase means being exposed to fewer new cards (though not none; you'll still see a new villain card for instance), so that also diminishes the learning curve.  But the ultimate trump card in Megalopolis's favor is Rooftop Combat, since it basically turns the Environment deck off altogether, possibly for several turns, and thus reduces the distraction of having to pay attention to more than just the villain.  Once the players are experienced, Megalopolis begins to be boring and frustrating, but to the newbie, it's the best Environment for simplifying the choices they must face in ignorance, letting them concentrate on mastering the new concepts one or two at a time.

(Of course, ease of play is only a point in favor of a newbie game; raw cool factor is another one, and so I might well use Insula Primalis for a newbie environment; everybody loves lava and dinosaurs.)

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Rooftop Combat is certainly a (usually) helpful card due to its shutdown of the environment deck, provided the villain doesn't have so many damaging cards out that the damage bonus doesn't add up to something tremendous. Once we had it come up in the first round against the Dreamer, which was just epic as it meant we had a damage bonus to kill all the projections and could completely ignore the environment deck for the entire game :D.

Personally I would say that having to skip certain phases (which would keep changing as you get rid of one card only for a different one to come up and make you skip something else instead) would probably be confusing, especially for someone who hadn't had enough time to learn the turn phases just yet. I'd prefer to learn what it was I could do and get the hang of it before something started teling me I couldn't do one or more of the things. Still, people differ, so I'm sure there are those who wouldn't be too bothered by it…though there is the other matter of that having to keep skipping phases (if you keep drawing those kind of cards round after round so there's always something you can't do) is basically giving the villain a huge advantage and a game you might otherwise have won without too much trouble can become a rather swift and horrible wipe due to the fact that you couldn't get yourselves going enough to take down whatever the villain is putting out. I've had this happen in games and I reckon it'd be really frustrating to a new player - "Okay so you're playing Ra because he's pretty straightforward and just nukes stuff…except on this turn you can't play any cards so you can't put out that lovely Staff of his…okay, this round you now can't use any base powers so you can't use your now-boosted Pyre skill…and now you can't draw cards so that Living Conflagration is actually now worse than your base power…" and so on. Worse if multiple you-can't-do-that-thing cards are out at once, but hopefully if you're showing a newbie the game you're not going up against someone like the Chairman where that's more likely to happen ;).

My newbie environment of choice is Insula Primalis. Did it on Monday, in fact, when showing a friend the game for the first time. Baron Blade in Insula Primalis. I playe as Legacy and Visionary, so as to give damage buffs (and explain the Nemesis mechanic) and keep Blade's deck under control (good thing I did - the remaining two Mobile Defence Platforms were right next to each other within a couple of cards of the top) without ending up doing loads of damage and risking "taking over" the game. I gave Ra to my friend because as mentioned above, I find him straightforward and you can do All of the Things (ie benefit via both one-shots and ongoings, plus you even have one equipment card) whilst nuking the crap out of everything :). By the end of the (victorious) game Ra was buffed by Galvanise, Inspiring Presence, Imbued Fire, and two Obsidian Fields. He didn't manage to get the Staff out (though had a Summon Staff but didn't get a chance to use it before the game ended), but as he was already doing eight damage with his Blazing Inferno this didn't matter hugely, considering who we were fighting :). We then fought Ambuscade with different heroes and thrashed him too - I could have got the killing blow but I let my friend do it and he strung a load of cards together (was playing TLT though used Research Grant rather than the base power for every round except one) to take out pretty much all the environment targets before finishing off Ambuscade himself. And he's coming round in a couple of hours to play some more :).

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
I haven't used Megalopolis with any face-to-face players for the very reasons Ameena mentions. The thing that I find important to drum into new players is the Play-Power-Draw sequence, and skipping one of those phases (and then potentially skipping a different one next turn) I beleive would interfere with getting that basic principle down.

Besides, I'm trying to show off how fun this game is. It's much less fun if you can't do all of the cool stuff you're supposed to be able to do...

Insula Primalis all the way for me.

posts.cooked: Insula is one of the best environment decks, it doesn't mess with you, it just tries to eat you.  I can respect that.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
Since we are talking about Megaopolis, let me tell you about my quick game last night.

Advanced Dawn. In Megaopolis. Team was Tempest Haka and Dark Visionary.

Dawn started the game with Blood and Tears. Anvil was the first card played.

Megaopolis' play order was as follows: Hostage Situation, Traffic Pile Up, Hostage Situation, Impending Casualty

After the second Hostage Situation, Sweat showed up.

Dawn never got touched, no citizens ever got put down, and it ended in 4 rounds with no hero having cards in hand.

Megaopolis shut me down hard. I had to do a rematch with the same setup in which I ended up squeaking out a win (thank you Brain Burn!).

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: Ouch. Nasty! We once had a game versus Dawn where she had Sweat and Tears in play after the first turn, meaning we only had half our starting cards on our first turns and never managed to get set up to the extent that we could really start doing anything. Another time we were in Megalopolis against…someone (may even have been Dawn again) and were doing okay - we all had reasonable stuff available, the villain wasn't being a massive threat, and none of us were particularly near to being dead. Then the environment chained all three different horrible cards turn after turn after turn, for ages, so even though we were getting rid of them every round we were repeatedly shut down in various phases of our turns and subsequently lost the game. Had Megalopolis not done what it did, we were well on track for a relatively easy win (assuming the villain didn't later do anything disastrous for us, but since I can't remember for sure who it was, I don't know how likely that would've been).

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked: Dawn has produced some legendary games in my time - my very first battle against her, she opened on Blinding Blast, so we were all down two cards on turn 1, and by the end of the game, my decision to keep Return with the Dawn around, and thus render Citizens Sweat and Tears immortal, had resulted in Tachyon being completely neutralized (no cards in hand, could not draw enough cards to keep any in hand, no Ongoings in play) and Ra reduced to nothing but his base power.  Only Wraith had Equipment on the table and was able to directly slice Dawn into pieces 8 HP at a time.  Dawn never flipped that game, and experience has taught me that the game is much easier (and more importantly quicker) when that's the case...she's one of the few heroes that I think is easier to fight with 3 heroes than 5, because she gets fewer Citizens out and thus it's more likely to be safe for you to just ignore them.  Plus her innate attack deals less damage, and if she does flip she won't stay flipped for long.  I believe I once had a solitaire game against Dawn which took seven hours to play out (admittedly, my attention was partially on the Internet, so it shouldn't have taken that long, but the actual play part was probably not less than three hours).  So much waiting, so much math...it's just easier not to let her flip, if you can afford that luxury.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: We just make sure we have one Citizen (usually Spring) around before we make our fifth kill. Then again, with H=3, we don't have to have any more than that so I suppose it's easier. So generally we don't have to worry about her staying flipped because of the whole flip-and-insta-flip back thing :).

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
If I've kept count correctly, the game I just finished was #67 in my time playing SOTM, and it also marks the moment at which I have played every hero exactly twelve times.  So it's time for more factoids from my datasheet.

* Absolute Zero still holds the death record - he's only survived to the end of the game four times.  However, he's been involved in victories for his team half the time; the record for game losses involving a single hero remains with Fanatic, who (despite my friend Chris's record of winning games with her) has only helped to win six of the games she's been in, and only one of those involved her dying - her other six failures were a gift she chose to share with the group.  At this point I'm forced to wonder if I'm subconsciously sabotaging her.  (Expatriette continues to be tied with Fanatic for second-most deaths, but has won the game once more while dying in the process.)

* On the other end of the spectrum, Nightmist continues to hold the best survival record, having only been incapacitated in one game.  She and Omnitron-X have both won all but one of the games they've played in!  (Omnix died in two of these victories, but I've also seen another player run him to good effect, while I'm the only player in my circle of IRL friends that has tried Nightmist.  This doesn't include members of the forum games crew in games that I wasn't involved in, of course, any more than it includes RL games from before I started playing.)  Visionary and Scholar have only ever actually lost the game once, dying 2 and 3 times respectively, but they have also each been involved in one game which was conceded as a loss, after they were the only hero who survived and had clearly no hope of achieving a turnaround (this is different from conceding a game just out of lack of desire to continue it, without recognizing it as a win or a loss).  Interestingly, Visionary's concession comes from the same game in which Nightmist died...all the deck-control both heroines wield wasn't enough to turn that game around.

* The Ennead is the only villain I have not fought at least three times.

* Plague Rat is the only villain who I have not played three heroes against.  Akash'Bhuta is the only one I haven't played four heroes against.  (Multiple five-hero games are still in my future.)

* Iron Legacy has beaten me three times.  Spite has frustrated me into a concession (a not-win/loss one, that is) once, but never actually incapped one of my heroes, nor has Plague Rat or Akash'Bhuta, all in exactly three games.  So IL has defeated all my heroes (except once the Scholar) in as many games as the other three have failed to kill even one.

* I have played in every environment six times, except for Rook City, Pike Industrial, the Time Cataclysm, and the Tomb of Anubis (the latter is the only one that remains at just four plays).  The Realm of Discord is the only one where I have lost three games, and abandoned a fourth in disgust; I have won only two games there, as well as two of the four in the Tomb, making IR clearly the site of my greatest frustrations.  The Final Wasteland is the safest place in the world as far as I can tell; uniquely among environments, I've never lost a game there, and only had one hero even incapped.

* Of the 91 possible combinations of two heroes, the only ones I have yet to see in a game involving myself are Mr. Fixer + Tempest (ironic, given that art has shown the latter two together on several occasions), Mr. Fixer + Bunker, Bunker + Scholar, Omnitron-X with either Haka or Wraith, Wraith + Chrono-Ranger, and Absolute Zero with either Argent Adept or Chrono-Ranger.  (I seem to be prone to repeating combinations with these specific heroes for some reason.)  In addition to these eight matches I haven't seen are eleven where I have not played both heroes, totaling 72 of the possible combinations which I have explored.  (The number of combinations of two- and three-hero groups with each other or with additional single heroes is...rather larger, and I won't be making significant headway on it anytime soon.)
